name: Project Ecommerce
tagline: Event-driven storefront split into six bounded contexts
summary: A storefront broken into six independently deployable Spring Boot services, each
owning its own data: auth issues and validates tokens, catalog holds the product
tree, stock reserves and releases inventory, order runs the purchase saga, payments
settles transactions, and customers keeps the identity record.
A BFF sits in front and composes the reads the web client needs, so the browser
never fans out across six services to render a single page.

name: Library Management
summary: A library domain modelled end to end: titles and copies, member registration,
lending with due dates, and returns with penalty rules.
Built across several iterations as the modelling got sharper — the later repos
carry the domain logic the earlier ones only sketched.

name: People Operations
tagline: HR domain: employees, org structure and records
summary: Employee lifecycle handled as its own domain: hiring records, org structure,
role changes and terminations, with the audit trail HR processes require.
Two takes on the same problem — one procedural, one domain-driven — kept side
by side to compare how the model holds as rules accumulate.

name: Microservices Lab
tagline: Ordering flow used to test integration patterns
summary: A deliberately small ordering flow — catalogue, order, receipt — used as a bench
for integration patterns: synchronous versus event-driven calls, idempotency,
retry and compensation.
Small enough that a pattern's cost is visible instead of buried in domain code.

name: Platform Foundations
tagline: Service template and the infrastructure it ships on
summary: The starting point for new services and the infrastructure that runs them:
a Spring Boot template carrying the conventions worth repeating, and Terraform
describing the AWS footprint those services land on.
